Triggers.value: Similar weather conditions to when the event happened

Maladaptive Strategies.value: keep mind occupied all the time

Threat.value: I listen for sounds that might mean someone is entering my home
My body reacts to danger before I have even had time to think
I jump or startle at ordinary sounds that would not bother most people

Memory.value: The memory is so extreme it is hard to believe it actually happened to me
When I think about the frightening event I can sometimes smell things that I smelt when the frightening event happened.
The memory feels like it belongs to someone else rather than to me

Negative Appraisals.value: The world is a dangerous place
I am no longer capable of doing the things that defined me
I can no longer trust my own body

vignette: Lena, a 42-year-old African woman and former factory worker, has been struggling with persistent psychological distress since she was subjected to torture several years ago. The traumatic event took place on a chilly December evening when Lena was returning home from work. She remembers the cold, crisp air and the smell of damp earth that filled her nostrils as she walked through a deserted alleyway. On that night, Lena encountered a group of individuals who had been tracking her for months due to her involvement in a local community activism group. They abducted her and brought her to an abandoned warehouse where she was held captive and subjected to severe physical and psychological torture over the course of several days. The memory of that cold December weather and the overwhelming scent of damp earth has since become a potent trigger, making it nearly impossible for Lena to walk through certain areas without feeling overwhelmed by fear. Since the event, Lena's life has been marked by a series of maladaptive strategies and avoidance behaviors. She frequently wears heavy makeup to mask any visible signs of trauma on her face and tries to keep her mind occupied all the time to avoid intrusive thoughts about the torture. This constant mental distraction has led to significant fatigue and reduced efficiency at work, causing tension with her colleagues. Lena also avoids wearing clothes that remind her of the event, which has limited her wardrobe choices significantly. At home, she remains hyper-vigilant, always listening for sounds that might indicate someone is entering her house. Her body reacts instinctively to perceived threats, and even ordinary sounds can startle her, sending waves of panic through her system. The memory of the traumatic event itself feels surreal and almost alien to Lena. She finds it difficult to believe that such extreme events happened to her, and the olfactory recall often brings back vivid yet disorienting sensations of damp earth and cold air, making her question whether these memories are truly hers or if they belong to someone else. Lena's negative appraisals have fundamentally altered how she views herself and the world around her. She now sees the world as a dangerous place where threats lurk around every corner. This belief has led her to withdraw from social activities and isolate herself, further exacerbating her sense of vulnerability. Additionally, Lena feels that she is no longer capable of performing tasks that once defined her as a factory worker and community activist, leading to significant self-doubt and diminished confidence in her abilities. The combination of these symptoms has taken a heavy toll on Lena's daily life. Her relationship with her ex-husband deteriorated due to her increasing isolation and difficulty engaging in normal activities together. At work, she is no longer as productive or engaged, which has strained relationships with her colleagues and supervisors. Despite the intensity of her symptoms, it was only recently that Lena decided to seek help. A particularly distressing incident at work triggered a panic attack that left her unable to function for several days. This experience made her realize that she needed professional support to manage her symptoms effectively and reclaim some control over her life. Her primary fear is that the trauma will continue to dictate every aspect of her existence, while her hope lies in finding ways to mitigate its impact and rebuild a sense of safety and self-efficacy. Lena's current state reflects a complex interplay between her traumatic experiences, her cognitive appraisals, and her maladaptive coping strategies. Her journey towards healing will require addressing these various dimensions through evidence-based therapeutic interventions aimed at reducing distress, enhancing resilience, and restoring her belief in the possibility of a fulfilling life beyond the shadow of trauma.
